shared_anchors: Flooding at Save the Chimps sanctuary in Fort Pierce, St. Lucie County
Staff rely on tractors, trailers and off-road vehicles to navigate the flooded property
Drone-assisted delivery of food during the flooding
novel_facts: Facilities director Mark Yohannan says nearly 15 golf carts have broken down
The sanctuary requests temporary taller four-wheel-drive vehicles and financial donations
Staff plan to raise their concerns at a St. Lucie County Commission meeting next week
Yohannan reports 19 inches of rain and the worst flooding in the sanctuary's 25 years in Fort Pierce
material_update_promotion_decisions.reason: Both articles cover the same sanctuary flooding and disrupted animal-care operations. The incoming report adds equipment counts, recovery needs and a planned appeal to commissioners, but no consequential government action, changed animal status or distinct accountability development. These are additional operational and recovery details, not a material update or independently newsworthy follow-up.
